title: Towards Real-world Human Behavior Simulation: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Long-horizon, Cross-scenario, Heterogeneous Behavior Traces

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the positive prediction rate (the proportion of positive outcomes among all interactions) and comparing the interaction probabilities of LLM-simulated users against the inherently sparse baselines of real human behaviors.

Comparing emotional expressions and language styles in customer service dialogues by applying an LLM-based sentiment judge and evaluating five dimensions of computational politeness (politeness markers, hedging, blame avoidance, emotional control, and face-saving strategies).

Analyzing intra-user and inter-user behavioral distances using a 17-dimensional feature vector of positive action rates to measure whether LLMs preserve individual-specific behavioral heterogeneity or converge to an average persona.
